about.title: Perris Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Perris sits at a busy crossroads in Riverside County, where commuter traffic, freight movement, and neighborhood streets meet every day. In 2025, the city's final public record shows 267 injury collisions, 395 people injured, and 6 traffic deaths among a population of roughly 75,000. The corridors that appear most often in those reports are Perris Boulevard, 4th Street, and the Ramona Expressway, and crashes tend to cluster on Mondays in the mid-afternoon window between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. If you were hurt in one of those collisions, the days that follow usually bring more questions than answers: who covers the car, who pays the emergency room bill, and why an adjuster you have never met wants to record a conversation. We handle car accident cases in Perris and can help take one task off your list. We work on contingency, meaning nothing comes out of your pocket up front and no fee is owed unless your case results in a recovery. You describe what happened once; our team can evaluate it and guide you forward.

items.title: The clock is shorter than most people think
items.desc: California gives you two years to file most car accident claims, but if a city, county, or state vehicle was involved, or if a road condition is part of the story, a government claim may be due in as little as six months. Getting started early keeps those options open.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even a driver who is found partly responsible can still recover, reduced by their share. We can push back when an insurer tries to assign you more blame than the facts support.

items.question: The other driver's insurer already called me. Should I give them a recorded statement?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and it is usually wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Recorded answers given while you are still in pain or unsure of details can be used later to reduce your claim. Politely take down the adjuster's name and let a lawyer handle that conversation.

items.question: My crash was on the Ramona Expressway. Does it matter that it is a county road?
items.answer: It can. Portions of the Ramona Expressway fall under public agency control, and if a roadway defect, signal problem, or government vehicle contributed to the collision, a separate claim against that entity may need to be filed within six months rather than two years. Our team can sort out which rules apply to your specific crash location and who the responsible parties are.

items.question: What should I save from the scene of a Perris car accident?
items.answer: Keep everything: photos of the vehicles and the roadway, the CHP or Perris police report number, contact details for any witnesses, and every medical record and receipt. Preserve your car in its damaged state until it has been documented, and write down your own account of what happened while it is fresh. Evidence fades quickly on busy corridors like Perris Boulevard, so the sooner it is gathered, the better.
